memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Joseph gave orders to fill their bags with grain, to put each man's silver back in his sack, and to give them provisions for their journey. After this was done for them, they loaded their grain on their donkeys and left." - Gen 42:25-26 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
As the brothers prepare to leave, Joseph secretly does something remarkable. He orders that their bags be filled with grain, that provisions be given for the journey — and that the silver they paid be quietly returned to each man's sack. They came to buy food, and they are given the food and their money back, without even knowing it. Grace was tucked into their grain sacks, hidden and unearned.

Think about who received this kindness: the very brothers who had sold Joseph for silver years before. Now Joseph, instead of taking their silver, gives it back to them. Where they had once profited from betraying him, he now blesses them freely. This is grace — undeserved kindness poured out on those who had wronged him.

There is a picture of the gospel in this. We come to God empty and needy, expecting to have to earn or pay our way — and He gives us not only what we need but far more, returning to us what we could never have deserved. God's grace is often hidden in unexpected places, given quietly to those who least deserve it, including us.

And there is a challenge here too. Joseph blessed those who had wronged him. Are we willing to do the same — to return kindness for injury, to bless those who have hurt us? "Do not repay evil with evil... but with blessing" (1 Pet 3:9). Let us be people who hide grace in others' sacks, freely giving what was never earned.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I received grace from God that I could never have earned?
2. Am I willing to return kindness to those who have wronged me?
3. Where can I quietly bless someone who does not "deserve" it?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You for the grace You hide in my life, giving me far more than I deserve. Help me to pour out that same undeserved kindness on others, even those who have wronged me. Amen.
